quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes driving dangerous.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and either rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and either rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour during long trips. Share driving with another person so you can both rest safely.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles and continuously pass cars on a two-lane road, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass, your risk of a crash increases.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: It is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean you cannot pass. These areas have poor visibility, making passing unsafe.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat. Airbags can seriously injure young children.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:

options.text: Play loud music while driving to distract yourself.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to release anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect your ability to drive safely. Calm down before driving so you can focus on the road.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and its effects.

questions.question: If you see animals standing near the road while driving, you should:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and proceed carefully. Animals may suddenly move into the road. There may also be other animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about a crosswalk where pedestrians cross. When you see this sign, slow down and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You may see this sign at intersections where oncoming traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross the street in the middle instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally. Stop for them no matter where they are crossing.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and harder to see than adults. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Be aware that children on bicycles may suddenly come onto the road.

questions.question: When you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you continue.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out and flag down the first vehicle that passes.
Move off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you stop on an interstate, move to the shoulder. Turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of the high-speed traffic.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else, like eating or drinking caffeine, speeds up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign tells you that traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to allow these vehicles to merge safely.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs affect many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, lower alertness, and hurt your ability to concentrate.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving gets worse. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and the movement of other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Get ready. Traffic will merge into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready. Traffic will merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must also always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas in your vision that appear when you are tired.
Areas near your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas near your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder. Check the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic rules.
Only if the traffic light favors them.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic rules.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area or service station. Take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe substitutes for real rest and can make driving more dangerous.
